conviction_note: The only item I found that the two-analyst bar probably lacks is a ~$6.2M IEEPA refund contingency that the 10-K left unrecognised while CBP's CAPE programme was paying out through the quarter. It is worth roughly +$0.10 to +$0.25 of EPS against -$3.42, and it is a one_off on a stock that trades on the FY27 guide, with a reaction history of 12% median alternating moves. So the number is a near-zero +0.3, not a call.

positioning_check: Short interest 2,065,824 shares at the 2026-08-31 settlement, up 37% from 1,507,725. That is 12.56% of float and 7.6 days to cover per MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/SCHL/short-interest, fetched 2026-09-24), or 14.04% of float and 6.71 days per stockanalysis (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/schl/statistics/). The shorts built into a -14.3% 20-day drawdown with no filed cause. There is no usable skew: the chain is unusable, with 31 contracts of open interest and the ATM spread at 94% of mid. Put/call OI of 1.58 on that tiny open interest means nothing. The short is crowded enough that I would shrink any negative, and I have none.

findings.finding: The FY26 10-K says about $9.0M of Scholastic's tariff payments fall under the February 2026 IEEPA ruling. $2.8M had been received and recognised by 2026-05-31, and the rest (about $6.2M) was left unrecognised as a gain contingency under ASC 450. CBP's CAPE refund process opened Phase 2 on 2026-06-29 and by 2026-08-21 had certified about 64% of the refund pool for disbursement. So some or all of the $6.2M plausibly landed inside Q1 (June to August). The FY26 non-GAAP reconciliation does not list the $2.8M among excluded items, so a Q1 receipt would probably flow into adjusted results: about +$4.6M after tax, or roughly +$0.10 to +$0.25 per share on about 18.9M shares, against a -$3.42 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior SCHL print has turned on a below-the-line item. In Sept 2025 the stock fell 12% after the Q1 FY26 release, when adjusted EPS of -$2.52 missed a -$2.45 bar by about 3%, revenue missed (actual $225.6M) and Education fell 28%. That was a revenue and segment story, not an EPS one. In Dec 2025 an adjusted-EPS beat was sold on weak EBITDA guidance. This name does not pay for EPS quality on a seasonal loss quarter; it pays for the guide.
findings.source_date: 2026-07 (FY2026 10-K, period ended 2026-05-31; IEEPA paragraph read from search snippet of the filing)
findings.why_not_priced: Only two analysts cover the name, and their EPS range is -$3.15 to -$3.69, with Sidoti cutting its Q1 to -$3.15 from -$3.11 and not raising it. A modelled refund would show as a narrower loss than last year's comparable-basis trend; instead consensus is $0.90 worse than last year's -$2.52, which dilution from a smaller share count and sale-leaseback rent roughly explain on their own. The recognition policy sits in a 10-K footnote, not in the wire copy.
findings.independence: CBP disbursement progress from a different source: https://www.tariffstool.com/tariff-refund-tracker (and the CAPE phase dates at https://www.ghy.com/trade-compliance/cbp-cape-ieepa-refund-progress/). The FY26 non-GAAP reconciliation, which excludes no tariff item, is at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866729/000086672926000015/fy26q4pressrelease.htm. Timing of Scholastic's own receipt is inferred, not documented.

Cause of the -14% drawdown since late August: the only dated items are the Estate sale to the company at $39.76 (8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866729/000119312526371245/schl-20260827.htm), a 2026-09-04 -5.1% day on low volume with no stated cause, and the short build. I treated the unexplained drawdown as 0.

Scholastic Education Platform launch at back-to-school 2026: no customer complaints found.
McGraw Hill's fiscal Q1 2027 (to June 30): K-12 up, but it is core curriculum and not a clean read-through to supplemental.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. A 20-day run-up of -14.3% with shorts up 37% says the market is leaning negative into a quarter whose revenue bar is pinned to the company's own pre-guide. My one small positive runs against that lean, but it is too small and too far below the line to argue the lean is wrong, and the price already reflects everything else I found.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0; positioning and a two-analyst bar are the information set, not a finding): dropped the draft's +1.0 positioning finding. That finding argued that consensus pinned to the company guide plus a 37% short build made last September's miss mechanism less likely. It is now recorded in positioning_check only.

Lesson 2 (tariff refunds landed in four names and the move split on guidance): cut the IEEPA refund from +0.5 to +0.3. It is a one_off with no stated path to the FY27 guide, and if it flows into adjusted results while the guide is only reaffirmed, the implied underlying number is weaker.

Lesson 1 (the reaction function has veto): print_vs_bar_pct moved from +0.5 to 0.0 on revenue, because I have no company-level evidence on Q1 revenue against a bar the company itself set. The EPS nudge from the refund is not a revenue beat.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage means a confirmed fact moves more) left the size alone. The refund's timing is inferred, not confirmed, so it is not the 'confirmed, unpriced' setup that lesson describes.
